picks.excerpt: Vercel released Agent Plugins 1.0.0, an open, vendor-neutral spec that packages Agent Skills and MCP servers into distributable plugins with a common directory structure and manifest. Design systems and UI conventions can now ship as portable agent skills across compatible clients.
picks.rationale: An open spec that lets a design system ship as a portable agent skill instead of a per-tool config.

picks.excerpt: The author found 127 design instances bound to raw colors instead of design-system tokens — all of which passed visual review until dark mode exposed them. The piece lays out how to constrain AI-generated UI to a closed token set with mechanical validation.
picks.rationale: A concrete, numbers-backed method for forcing AI-generated UI back onto a closed token set before dark mode exposes the drift.

picks.excerpt: Nekki shipped Cascadeur 2026.2 with a non-destructive animation layer system, easing controls and BVH import. Its AI inbetweening and Motion Generation systems were retrained on larger datasets, and an MCP server lets external LLM agents like Claude drive the animation tool.
picks.rationale: A shipping DCC app that hands its controls to an LLM agent over MCP — agentic workflow arriving in animation, not just code.

picks.excerpt: PTC introduced "Triple A" AI — Advise, Assist, Automate — in Creo 13, aimed at designer productivity inside the CAD product. "We want to make sure that the human is always in the loop," the company said of its AI-assisted modelling decisions.
picks.rationale: Mainstream CAD gets a named AI framework with a human-in-the-loop stance industrial designers will work under.

picks.excerpt: Takeaways from the 2026 State of CSS survey, including AI adoption: respondents who use AI generation 0–50% of the time outnumber heavier users 3,031 to 721. The author cautions the sample may skew less AI-dependent than the wider front-end population.
picks.rationale: Survey data on how much front-end work is actually AI-generated — a reality check against the hype curve.
